history.period: Antiquity uncertain; no published construction date (verify)
history.summary: Hilltop Shiva shrine in the Takhat Sagar hills near Kaylana Lake, about 10 km from Jodhpur. CONFLICTING ORIGIN TRADITIONS (flagged, unverified): one travel source says the temple was built by 'King Siddha of the Rathore clan', hence the name Siddhanath; another local account says the isolated site was first settled by the hermit Veetragi Narain Swami and that a saint named Gaurishanker, known as Nepali Baba, personally built the stone temple by cutting rock. The approach is via the road right of the filter house on Jodhpur-Chopasani Road, then rock-cut steps. Reached by auto-rickshaw plus a short hike. No published construction date or builder consensus - verify with local temple records.

name: Siddhanath Shiv Temple
town_description: Jodhpur, the Blue City, is the second-largest city of Rajasthan and the historic capital of Marwar - home to Mehrangarh Fort, Kaylana Lake and a dense cluster of old temples, with an airport and major rail junction.

travel.road: Near Kaylana Lake in the Takhat Sagar hills; take the Jodhpur-Chopasani Road, turn right of the filter house, then climb rock-cut steps (verify route locally).

visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT: some sources say open 10 AM-2 PM daily, others say open daylight hours with no fixed timings (verify on site).
